one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window to 2026-11-05. (1) Ericsson Q3 2026 report on 2026-10-15 [9]: Ericsson already said it expects continued pressure on Networks margins in Q3 and is acting on component-cost inflation [8], so a read-through on RAN pricing and memory costs is likely mildly negative-to-neutral; Dell'Oro says the RAN market is flat for 2026 [6]. (2) Nokia's own Q3 2026 report on 2026-10-22 [3] - inside the window. Nokia pre-guided Q3 sales +3-7% q/q and comparable operating profit 'largely flat' vs Q2's EUR 434m because of software revenue phasing, with a 'meaningful increase in Q4' [1][5], so the headline OP is pre-announced; the swing factors are AI & Cloud order intake (Q2 EUR 2.8bn), supply constraints (CEO: 'if there was more supply... we'd probably generate more revenue') and memory cost pass-through [5]. Nokia's last two prints moved the stock sharply both ways (week of Q1 print +27%, week of Q2 print -10% per weekly closes [28]). Today's +6.3% jump adds some short-term reversal risk. I therefore use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at $10.75 (slightly below today's $10.84) with a 17% monthly sigma (62% annual vol / 3.5 = 17.7%, kept at full width because earnings fall inside the window). No directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of 65% P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 EUR 0.42 x 20x = EUR 8.40 = $9.46 at EUR/USD 1.12605) and 35% DCF (2028 FCF EUR 2.10bn capitalised at 9.5%-3.5% = EUR 35.0bn + EUR 4.3bn net cash over 5.80bn diluted shares = EUR 6.78 = $7.63) -> $8.82 per ADS (1 ADS = 1 share).

bear.story: AI & Cloud backlog converts slowly because of memory/indium-phosphide supply constraints, component inflation squeezes Mobile Infrastructure margins (Ericsson and Calix already flag memory costs [8][11]), RAN stays flat [6]; 2027 OP ~2.3bn, NTM EPS ~EUR 0.36, multiple derates to ~15x (Ericsson-like 16.6x) -> EUR ~5.5 = ~$6.2.

base.story: Nokia hits its 2026 guide and tracks toward the upper half of the 2028 EUR 2.7-3.2bn OP target; NTM EPS ~EUR 0.42; market keeps a modest AI premium (~21x, near peer median) -> EUR ~8.8 = ~$9.9. Fundamental fair value (~$8.8) sits below today's price, so base drifts down modestly.

bull.story: AI & Cloud doubles again (Q2 orders EUR 2.8bn vs sales 0.45bn), optical/DCI keeps compounding as Ciena (+35% FY26) and Dell'Oro (+16% market) indicate [7][10], AI-RAN goes commercial in 2027 [5]; 2028 OP run-rate >3.4bn, EPS ~EUR 0.50 at ~27x -> EUR ~13.3 = ~$15; approaches June-2026 high of $17.45.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 11.96x (RBBN) to 44.54x (ANET); EV/EBITDA 7.84x (ADTN) to 60.41x (CIEN). NOTE: the EV/EBITDA figures in ev_ebitda_fwd are TTM (trailing) from Stock Analysis, the only verified source reachable; no verified forward EV/EBITDA was available, so EV/EBITDA is used only as a cross-check, not as a valuation method. The peer set splits into slow telecom vendors (ERIC 16.6x, RBBN 12.0x, HPE 14.7x) and AI-networking names (CIEN 41.8x, ANET 44.5x, GLW 43.0x).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 20x NTM P/E, just below the 20.76x peer median and well inside the range; Nokia itself trades at 24.0x forward P/E and 18.7x TTM EV/EBITDA [13], i.e. above the median on P/E.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium applied. A slight discount to the median is justified by mix: ~73% of Q2 sales are to telecom providers (EUR 3,514m of 4,815m [2]) in a RAN market Dell'Oro projects flat for 2026 [6], where the closest peer Ericsson trades at 16.6x with negative 3Y EPS growth forecasts; only ~9% (AI & Cloud EUR 446m) is in the high-growth AI segment that justifies Ciena/Arista-type multiples. Nokia's company targets (2028 OP 2.7-3.2bn from ~2.4bn 2026) imply ~10-13%/yr OP growth, below the peer median 3Y EPS growth forecast.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$6.30 (EUR ~5.6) the market would be pricing Nokia at Ericsson-like ~15x on ~EUR 0.37 EPS, i.e. abandoning the 2028 OP target and the AI & Cloud backlog conversion; that level is also roughly where the stock traded before the AI re-rating (Jan 2026 weekly closes $6.4-6.8 [28]). Trading there would most likely mean an order/backlog problem (AI & Cloud orders not converting, hyperscaler capex pause) or a margin break from component costs rather than ordinary 62%-vol noise.

reasoning: Lane: industry. Chain evidence is mixed: optical/DCI demand is very strong (Dell'Oro optical +16% in 2026, DCI +40% y/y in 1Q26, Nokia a top-4 optical vendor [7]; Ciena FQ3 revenue +37%, FY26 guide +35% [10]), consistent with Nokia's AI & Cloud sales +103% and EUR 2.8bn Q2 orders [1][2]. But the larger mobile side is flat: Dell'Oro sees 2026 RAN broadly flat [6], Ericsson's organic sales fell 1% and it flags component-cost inflation and Q3 Networks margin pressure [8], and Calix shows memory costs hitting gross margin [11]; Nokia's CEO confirms supply constraints and memory pricing [5]. Fundamentally I anchor on the company's 2028 OP target (EUR 2.7-3.2bn [4]), placed slightly above midpoint for AI momentum, giving NTM EPS ~EUR 0.42 at Oct-2027; at a peer-median-like 20x (peer median 20.76x across 11 networking/optical/telecom comps) that is $9.46, and a DCF at 9.5%/3.5% gives $7.63; blended fair value $8.82, about 19% below today's $10.84 (all EUR->USD at 1.12605, Twelve Data, cross-checked against the Helsinki line). The market currently pays 24x forward [13] for the AI narrative, and sell-side average target is $14.97 [25], so I don't put the median at fair value: scenarios bear $6.2 (25%) / base $9.9 (50%) / bull $15.0 (25%), mean ~$10.3. The ladder is a blend of that scenario mixture with a lognormal (median ~$9.9, sigma ~0.52, a bit below the 62% realized vol since the 2026 vol included the AI re-rating spike), giving a ladder median of ~$9.8 and P(>= $10.84) = 0.42. Research was partly limited: nokia.com and several news pages returned 403, so Nokia figures come from the EDGAR 6-K and the stock-exchange-release mirror; Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data statistics/estimates required a paid plan, so consensus 2027/28 EPS was not available and peer EV/EBITDA is trailing.
